chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurārah ibn A'yan, who said:
We asked Abā Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who forgets the qunūt until he bows. He said: He should perform the qunūt after the ruku'. But if he does not remember, then there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir عليه السلام, the Imam being asked for the ruling
key_terms.الْقُنُوتَ: the supplicatory invocation recited in salat (prayer) at its designated place
key_terms.بَعْدَ الرُّكُوعِ: after the bowing, indicating the missed qunūt may be made up then
key_terms.فَلَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: there is no obligation, penalty, or blame upon him if he does not remember
key_terms.يَرْكَعَ: to enter ruku', the bowing posture in salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets the qunūt until after bowing in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding one who forgets the qunūt in salat (prayer) until reaching ruku'. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that the qunūt may be performed after the ruku', and if it is not remembered at all, no liability or penalty applies.
